shell.title: Humanities & Translation
shell.description: Choose a track for close reading, argument practice, or translation inside the same HanziHome workspace.

descriptions.poetry: Read each work layer by layer: original text, language, poetics, interpretation, and practice.
descriptions.history: Read source texts, connect claims to evidence, and distinguish verifiable information from interpretation.

guide.poetryWhy: Poetry practice helps you read compressed sentences, notice omitted subjects and older meanings, track imagery, and compare translations that preserve meaning but differ in rhythm and nuance.
guide.historyWhy: History and thought practice trains you to separate what a text actually says from later interpretation, while checking evidence and the limits of inference.
guide.poetryStart: Start with four-line poems and read one layer at a time; advanced prosody is not required at the beginning.
guide.historyStart: Start with short passages and parables; learn to ask questions before moving into complex chronology.
guide.poetryMethod: Separate the original text, line-by-line meaning, imagery, and translation before guessing the author’s intended message.
guide.historyMethod: Start with three labels: verifiable information, interpretation, and claims that remain debated.
